To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

serial lead extraction, if it is performed with a very low complication rate, can reduce the risk of mortality in patients who have a long expected dwell time of an implantable cardioverter defibrillator lead.

serial lead extraction, compared with current practice of lead re-use, is associated with a lower procedural mortality in the long-term (≥5 year) management of indwelled implantable cardioverter defibrillators in young patients (>30 years expected dwell time) driven primarily by the high aggregate risk of lifetime lead malfunction.
the optimal management strategy for indwelling implant cardioverter-defibrilator leads is a function of patient age, lead longevity and lead complication rates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to manage the indwelling implant leads in implantable cardioverter defibrillators.
the optimal strategy for the management of indwell implantable cardioverter defibrillator leads in the context of the aging of the current generation of devices.
the optimal timing of lead removal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current strategy of lead reuse is appropriate for most patients, and serial lead extraction should be considered for younger patients with long expected indwell time.

the current practice of reuse of leads is the best strategy in the vast majority of cases, and the strategy of serial lead exchange at generator change should be limited to young patients with a high anticipated dwell time of the lead.
there is no clear advantage to prophylactic lead extraction at the time of generator change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a strategy of serial lead removal at time of generator replacement may be superior for young patients or those expected to have high dwell times of leads, whereas current practice is superior for older patients or those expected not to have a long dwell time of leads.

a serial lead exchange program should be reserved for those patients with high expected indwells, such as those who are young, have high risk of lead complications, and have a long expected device longevity.
a strategy of lead removal at the first opportunity is superior to a strategy of waiting until the lead fails, but only in young patients or those who are likely to have long-term lead dwell times.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal management of leads in the future is likely to be a function of lead longevity.
a prophylactic lead extraction strategy at time of generator replacement is superior in patients with long expected dwell times.

a strategy of serial lead removal is not universally better or worse than current practice, and it is important to consider individual patient characteristics in determining the best course of action.
